header.stance: 服務業走強、油價上升，推高美債實質殖利率

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 開篇固定收益論點

美國服務業需求走強、油價再漲，帶動6月3日美債殖利率上升，賣壓主要反映實質利率提高。10年期殖利率上升3個基點至4.49%，其中實質殖利率升4個基點，通膨補償反而微降。投資人重新評估聯準會需要多大的政策限制力，而不只是上調長期通膨預期。

勞動訊號仍不一致。ADP就業趨穩，兩項服務業調查的就業卻都萎縮；ISM訂單與活動更強，使市場繼續關注需求，褐皮書也描述能源成本正擴散至運輸、包裝、食品及肥料。達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan認為今年稍晚可能需要升息，John Williams則支持目前設定，但部分前提是能源市場能夠穩定。

債券與大盤股走弱，融資仍有序。美國財政部國庫券標售需求穩健，長端買回也用盡額度。QXO在訂單充裕下，以改善後的條件完成收購融資；AI借款則進一步拓展到市政債等市場。巴林甚至在遭受攻擊之際重新開啟波斯灣主權債發行，顯示定價與外部支持預期，對取得資金有多重要。

## 服務業需求推升實質殖利率

ISM服務業指數由53.6升至54.5，高於調查預期的53.7。商業活動達57.7、新訂單57.3，就業仍低於擴張門檻，為47.9；價格升至71.3，庫存跳升至追平紀錄的62.5。就業與價格低於部分預期時，美債短暫回升，之後市場轉而關注更強的整體數字與需求廣度，價格再度下跌。

ADP公布5月私人部門新增12.2萬人，略高於預測中位數，與週二強勁職缺數據共同呈現就業趨穩。S&P Global服務業終值較弱，由51.0降至50.7，就業減幅為2020年5月以來最大，企業信心也低迷。不過，新業務恢復成長，尚不足以支持需求全面萎縮的判斷。

4月工廠訂單增加4.8%，高於預期4.5%，前月修正後增加1.8%。出貨增1%、未完成訂單增1.7%、庫存增0.3%，其中運輸設備訂單大增21.6%至$1,311億，是主要動力。生產需求仍強，但成長集中於特定產業，又伴隨庫存增加，有多少能延續到最終支出仍有不確定性。

美伊再度交火，降低市場對區域供給迅速恢復的信心。WTI上漲2.41%至$96.02，Brent上漲1.89%至$97.81。褐皮書記錄的影響已不限燃料，運輸、包裝、食品及肥料成本都在增加；消費者不確定性與支出轉弱的跡象，則壓抑企業展望。

Logan認為金融情勢寬鬆，政策可能處於中性、甚至仍有刺激效果，限制力不足以完成通膨降溫。她將勞動市場形容為大致平衡，並表示今年稍晚可能需要升息。Williams認為目前利率適當，下一步沒有明確方向；他預期服務通膨放慢，部分仰賴中東能源市場穩定，以及第二輪效應有限。

接近收盤時，交換市場反映年底前升息0.25個百分點的機率超過80%，高於一週前60%，並完全反映2027年1月前行動。美國財政部長Scott Bessent提出不同看法，將4月CPI上漲3.8%描述為短期通膨波動，其他經濟數據則很強。他預期戰爭帶來一次性衝擊，與聯準會擔心成本更廣泛擴散的立場形成差距。

2年期殖利率上升3個基點至4.08%，5年期升4個基點至4.21%，10年期升3個基點至4.49%，30年期升2個基點至4.99%。2s10s維持41個基點，2s30s收窄1個基點至91個基點。過去一個月，2年期與5年期已分別上升20及19個基點，10年期升10個基點、30年期升2個基點；2s10s與2s30s同期分別收窄10及18個基點。

5年期名目殖利率的單日升幅最大。2s5s10s蝶式利差上升2個基點至負15個基點，2s10s30s升1個基點至負9個基點。實質殖利率方面，5年期升3個基點至1.68%，7年期升4個基點至1.89%，10年期升4個基點至2.11%，20年期及30年期各升3個基點至2.51%與2.72%。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點至2.38%，因此名目殖利率的升幅小於實質殖利率。

現金市場較平穩。4、6與8週國庫券附息等值殖利率各降1個基點，分別至3.68%、3.69%與3.69%；13、17與26週維持3.71%、3.74%及3.77%，52週則上升2個基點至3.82%。壓力較集中一年期及附息公債，而非最短天期現金工具。

美國財政部發行$690億119天期國庫券，最高得標貼現率3.635%，相當於投資利率3.730%，投標倍數3.15倍，最高得標利率配售比率93.35%，6月9日交割。流動性買回則用滿$20億上限，接受20至30年期名目附息公債；36檔合格券中有14檔獲接受，總報售金額$212.6億。買回於6月4日交割，已完成的操作有助非指標券流動性，但不改變淨舉債政策。

S&P 500下跌0.74%，Nasdaq 100跌0.29%，半導體卻上漲1.39%，延續AI相關支持。VIX上升1.84%至16.06，反應仍有限。美元指數上漲0.31%至99.53，黃金下降1.17%至$4,436.70。實質殖利率與美元上升，對多類資產造成壓力，但未見全面融資緊縮常伴隨的波動率急升或短券失序。

## AI借款拓展市場，QXO完成收購融資

QXO為收購TopBuild籌措的$60億融資，訂單超過需求三倍。$30億、7年期定期貸款取得至少$60億認購，利差收窄25個基點至基準加200個基點，發行價格改善至99.75。另$30億債券吸引$140億訂單，分為2031年及2034年到期兩部分，各$15億，按面額發行，殖利率分別6.5%及6.875%。

債券評等BB-，貸款BB+。即使都低於投資等級，收購融資供給稀缺，以及約$170億交易預期帶來的規模效益，仍協助QXO降低成本。摩根大通也在準備另一筆$18.5億收購貸款，支應Belden買下Ruckus Networks，金額約等於交易價值。融資已獲全額承諾，但尚未出售給機構投資人。

AI融資已遠超過個別資料中心債券。2025年初以來，美國投資等級債、高收益債、貸款及其他AI相關債務，累計發行超過$3,700億。紐約信用論壇與會者表示，需求仍強，尤其有獲利的超大規模雲端業者支持債務，或本金逐步攤還的安排；對僅仰賴未來成長預期的授信，則較謹慎。

摩根士丹利債務資本市場團隊估計，AI可能占今年全部信用市場發行的10%至15%。該行預測美國投資等級發行創紀錄達$2.25兆，高於去年的約$1.81兆，超大規模雲端業者預計籌資$2,500億至$3,000億。Alphabet已透過美元、加幣、歐元、英鎊、瑞郎及日圓發行約$600億。多幣別降低對單一買家的依賴，卻也使AI借款在債券、貸款及專案融資市場競逐更多資金。

Alphabet計畫參與一筆$10億加州預付能源市政債，開啟另一融資來源。初步文件列其為資金收受方，債券預期評等Aa2，將替Pioneer Community Energy取得折價長期電力。這種架構讓收受方享有免稅融資的經濟利益，投資人則取得高於相同評等市政債的收益，也將使美國科技公司進入先前主要由金融機構參與的市場。

其他需要資料中心電力的雲端巨擘可能跟進，但市政債市場遠小於全球企業債。供給增加時，合約保障、對手方信用與買家深度都會更重要；強大股東支持，也無法消除電力需求集中及依賴單一融資架構的風險。

Coastal GasLink準備發行C$10億兩部分投資等級債，約C$3億為11.25年期，C$7億約19年期，初步利差分別為政府債券加100及115個基點。加拿大債券到期付款帶來的再投資資金，可能有利需求，但最終規模與讓利尚未確定。

其他借款人的條件困難許多。Merlin Entertainments有逾€7.2億、約$8.38億的美元及歐元債券，將於2027年11月到期。3月淨債務約£54億，包含£16億租賃負債。第一季獲利弱、利息負擔重，家庭休閒支出也承壓，使部分債券接近困境價格；發行人評等已是CCC+。

Merlin可能選擇有擔保借款或提高部分債權順位的交換，更激進的資產移轉安排，則可能讓較優質的Legoland資產脫離既有債權人的追索範圍。股東支持與有需求的高收益債市場，提高交易完成機率，但改變順位只是重新分配回收價值，並不能解決獲利疲弱或槓桿過高。

信用主管對軟體貸款也更挑剔，特別關注以債付息曝險，同時私募股權股東規劃因應AI的防禦與進攻策略。Sleep Number另在準備可能的破產聲請，尋求日後可轉為破產保護期間融資的資金，先前曾討論約$5,000萬救援，4月初未償借款約$6.06億。這些公司的重點，已從一般再融資轉向優先順位救援資本。

聯準會指出，2025年銀行消費貸款、商用與住宅不動產貸款的逾放略增，但銀行資本仍充足。知名非銀行機構違約，也促使放款人重新檢查私人市場曝險的擔保品管理。另一些限制來自投資政策：管理逾$2,700億的瑞士機構，計畫讓特定石油生產商債券隨到期退出，不再新增購買。

政府殖利率上升、風險情緒較弱，帶動LQD下跌0.28%、HYG跌0.28%、JNK跌0.22%。QXO已完成的交易顯示，大額融資仍可能以更好條件成交；困境企業與投資限制的變化，則說明這個結果不能套用到每家發行人。

## 成長分歧，通膨壓力仍在

歐元區私人部門活動連續第二個月萎縮，綜合PMI終值由48.8降至48.5，服務業由47.6微升至47.7，仍低於50。新訂單轉弱、就業流失加速，投入及產出價格卻漲得更快。

生產者物價顯示成本已不只來自能源。4月月增0.6%、年增4.9%；扣除能源後月增0.9%，中間財升1.8%，能源反而跌0.4%。弱產出最終可能限制緊縮幅度，但更廣泛的成本增加，使歐洲央行難以單純等待。

日本央行總裁植田和男表示，6月15日至16日會議若認為通膨上行風險超過衝突對活動的傷害，就需要考慮升息。市場反映升息0.25個百分點機率約85%。儘管4月28日至5月27日已投入創紀錄的¥11.73兆干預，日圓仍在每$1兌¥160附近，美日利差與石油進口成本持續不利匯率。

日本核准¥3.1兆追加預算，包括初期用於限制汽油成本的¥2.5兆準備金。雖將以赤字融資債支應，但取消原先安排的發行後，全年市場供給總量不變，避免直接增加債券供給。補貼、弱勢日圓與央行減少購債，仍使通膨回應更複雜。本國殖利率提高，也可能減少日本機構對避險後外國債的興趣；匯率持續偏弱，則使干預與外匯準備管理仍需關注。

澳洲第一季GDP僅增0.3%，為前季速度的三分之一，低於預期。私人投資卻在資料中心帶動下增近4%，機械設備支出增加16%，家庭消費與淨出口則較弱。市場偏向預期澳洲央行暫停，3年期政府債券殖利率回落，但高單位勞動成本與油價仍保留再升息空間。

澳洲7年期標售取得超過發行額四倍的投標，出售A$10億2033年11月券，為該天期自前次標售以來最強投標倍數。成長轉弱加上目前殖利率，已吸引中期債買家，不必等央行宣布緊縮循環正式結束。

波蘭央行總裁Adam Glapinski表示，5月通膨3.1%、仍在目標區間內，3.75%政策利率已夠高。三個月後起算、為期三個月的遠期利率協議，比3個月參考利率高38個基點，低於戰爭開始後一度反映的74個基點緊縮。談話與定價下調，補充了前一天維持利率的決定。

中國服務業指數由52.6升至54.4，綜合指數由53.1升至54.0，需求改善、聘僱恢復、投入成本加速，售價卻大致持平。更強活動提供區域成長支持，暫時未見成本明顯轉嫁給客戶。

## 巴林重啟波斯灣融資，主權風險各異

巴林攔截伊朗飛彈與無人機數小時後，仍發行$10億10年期優先無擔保債，殖利率7.125%。訂單高峰超過$32億，使定價比初步約7.5%收窄37.5個基點，成為戰爭開始後波斯灣首筆公開主權債。

供給稀缺與區域支持預期，使融資在尚無穩定停火下重新開啟。巴林自身財務仍弱，公共債務約占GDP的140%，外匯準備偏低，荷莫茲海峽關閉又使石油收入幾乎消失。估計經濟將萎縮約4%，預算赤字超過GDP的8%。與阿聯的$54億貨幣交換強化外援假設，但成交殖利率仍顯示取得資金的成本。

阿根廷央行週三再買入$4,300萬後，超過全年$100億美元購買目標。創紀錄農產量、能源出口增加92%，以及省政府與企業海外借款，都支持流入。近期惠譽升評之際，主權利差也收窄，近期償債前景改善。

可用準備卻遠小於累計買入。總準備略高於$480億，按市價計的淨準備估計僅約$30億，因買入美元也用於償債。阿根廷在$200億IMF計畫最新審查中未達淨準備目標，2027年另有逾$300億付款到期。出口持續強勁可延長支付能力，重建淨準備仍不可少。

尚比亞債權人的反對，已形成阻擋部位。持有$13.6億2053年券逾25%的投資人，使買回案擬議的剩餘債券清理條款無法啟動。債券報價接近81美分，高於78美分要約。若IMF債務永續條件在6月及12月兩度達標，票息可能由0.5%升至7.5%；提前清償可降低未來成本，但高於要約的市價與阻擋部位，使協商條件更加重要。

印度融資壓力由債券擴散到銀行。戰爭以來10年期政府殖利率上升38個基點至7.04%，本地債券發行下降11%至₹10.9兆，企業轉向較便宜貸款。截至5月15日的一年，銀行信用成長16.2%，快於存款，6個月可轉讓定期存單利率5月跳升88個基點。企業仍能取得資金，更多風險卻移往短期銀行融資。

官員考慮取消或大幅調低外資債息20%稅率，並放寬部分證券持有上限。盧比今年貶值逾6%，收在每$1兌₹95.71，10年期殖利率另報7.02%。提案可能拓寬買家，但尚未通過，也不能單獨化解油價、匯率與銀行資金壓力。

匈牙利政治行情已進入兌現階段。Peter Magyar擊敗Viktor Orban以來，本幣債報酬超過11%，福林過去一年兌歐元升逾13%。要取得€164億歐盟資金，須在8月期限前完成專案。未來降息及信評調整可能帶來支持，但外幣債的大部分利多已反映。

迦納通膨連續第二個月上升，由3.4%升至3.7%，仍低於預測中位數4.3%。燃油及肥料推高食品價格，塞地今年貶值11%增加輸入壓力。總準備$140億可支付5.5個月進口，央行仍有空間平抑匯率波動。

政府將2026年成長預測由4.8%上調至逾6%，理由是通膨與利率下降，以及預算、外匯制度改革，年底通膨預測也由8%下調至5%。基礎改善反映2022年違約後的進展，但每年約$20億能源補助與食品再漲，仍限制財政。這組條件較支持維持14%政策利率，而非認定成長與準備增加已消除通膨風險。

美元與油價上升，新興市場美元債整體下跌，EMB跌0.37%。各國差異仍大：巴林成功但昂貴的發行、阿根廷準備增加，以及尚比亞合約與印度銀行融資壓力，分別影響債權人面對的風險。

## 前瞻市場意涵

6月4日08:30美東時間公布修正後生產力、單位勞動成本及初領失業救濟金，接續6月5日08:30就業報告，以及6月10日5月CPI。比較基準為生產力初值成長0.8%、單位勞動成本2.3%、前次初領21.5萬人、非農預期增加9.3萬人及失業率4.3%。若聘僱與成本仍強，之後服務或住宅通膨又普遍偏高，將支持實質利率上調；勞動明顯降溫、基本物價放慢，則會讓服務業調查的弱就業分項更有分量。

能源及政策決定這項壓力會擴散多遠。印度央行6月5日決策，加拿大央行6月10日，歐洲央行在下一週，日本央行6月15日至16日，聯準會6月16日至17日。荷莫茲海峽交通恢復、原油回落、能源進口國匯率轉強，可容許更耐心指引；運輸進一步受阻，或薪資、服務及預期壓力擴大，則使實質殖利率與跨境借款成本維持高檔。

6月4日美國財政部公告下週3、10與30年期附息公債，以及13、26週國庫券。當日13:40至14:00美東時間，進行上限$125億的一個月至兩年期附息債現金管理買回，6月5日交割。3年期標售在6月9日，10年期增額及另一筆17週國庫券在6月10日。Alphabet預付能源融資與Coastal GasLink兩部分發行，也提供企業端檢驗。國庫券穩定、交割順暢、交易不需大幅讓利就能維持規劃規模，將顯示新利率水準下仍有融資能力；投標疲弱或現金壓力，則會使供給成為下一波走勢更重要的因素。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Stronger US services demand and a renewed rise in oil pushed Treasury yields higher on June 3, with real rates accounting for the selloff. The 10-year yield rose 3 basis points to 4.49% as its real yield increased 4 basis points and inflation compensation edged down. Investors were reassessing how restrictive Fed policy needed to be, rather than simply marking up long-term inflation expectations.

The labor evidence remained mixed. ADP payrolls stabilized, while employment contracted in two services surveys. ISM's stronger orders and activity nevertheless kept the focus on demand, and the Beige Book described energy costs spreading through transport, packaging, food and fertilizer. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan saw scope for an increase later this year; John Williams favored the current setting, with his outlook partly dependent on energy stabilizing.

Financing remained orderly despite weaker bonds and broad equities. Treasury's bill auction drew solid demand and its long-end buyback used the full capacity. QXO completed a heavily subscribed acquisition package on improved terms, while AI borrowing reached further into municipal and other funding markets. Bahrain reopened Gulf sovereign issuance even amid attacks, showing how much access could depend on the price offered and expectations of support.

## Services Demand Drives Real Yields Higher

ISM services rose to 54.5 from 53.6, above a 53.7 survey forecast. Business activity reached 57.7 and new orders 57.3, while employment remained below the expansion threshold at 47.9. Prices increased to 71.3 and inventories jumped to a record-tying 62.5. Treasuries briefly recovered as employment and prices came in below some expectations, then sold off as investors focused on the stronger headline and breadth of demand.

ADP reported 122,000 additional private-sector jobs in May, slightly above the median forecast and consistent with stabilization after Tuesday's strong openings report. The final S&P Global services index gave a weaker signal, easing to 50.7 from 51.0 with the fastest employment decline since May 2020 and poor business confidence. New business returned to growth, however, limiting the case for a broad demand contraction.

Factory orders increased 4.8% in April, above a 4.5% forecast and after a revised 1.8% gain. Shipments rose 1%, unfilled orders 1.7% and inventories 0.3%. Much of the order strength came from transportation equipment, which surged 21.6% to $131.1 billion. Production demand remained firm, with sector concentration and stockbuilding leaving uncertainty over how much would carry through to final spending.

Renewed US-Iran exchanges reduced confidence in a quick restoration of regional supply. WTI gained 2.41% to $96.02 and Brent rose 1.89% to $97.81. The Beige Book described the consequences beyond fuel: transport, packaging, groceries and fertilizer costs were rising, while consumer uncertainty and weaker spending signs weighed on business outlooks.

Logan argued that financial conditions were accommodative and policy might be neutral or even supportive, rather than restrictive enough to finish bringing inflation down. She described labor conditions as broadly balanced and said an increase could be needed later in the year. Williams saw the current rate as appropriate and no obvious next direction. He expected services inflation to slow, partly on stabilization in Middle East energy and limited second-round effects.

By late trading, swaps assigned more than an 80% chance to a quarter-point increase by year-end, up from 60% a week earlier, with a move fully priced by January 2027. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent offered a different assessment, describing the April CPI increase of 3.8% as a short-term inflation blip and other economic data as very strong. His expectation of a one-off war-related shock contrasted with Fed concern about costs spreading more broadly.

The 2-year yield rose 3 basis points to 4.08%, the 5-year increased 4 to 4.21%, the 10-year added 3 to 4.49% and the 30-year rose 2 to 4.99%. The 2s10s curve held at 41 basis points and 2s30s flattened 1 to 91. Over a month, 2- and 5-year yields were up 20 and 19 basis points, against 10 at 10 years and 2 at 30 years; the corresponding 2s10s and 2s30s slopes had narrowed 10 and 18 basis points.

The 5-year sector bore the largest daily nominal increase. The 2s5s10s butterfly rose 2 basis points to -15 and 2s10s30s increased 1 to -9. Real yields climbed 3 basis points at five years to 1.68%, 4 at seven years to 1.89% and 4 at 10 years to 2.11%. Twenty- and 30-year real yields each rose 3 basis points to 2.51% and 2.72%. A 1-basis-point decline in the 10-year breakeven to 2.38% explained why the nominal yield rose less than the real yield.

Cash trading was calmer. Four-, six- and eight-week coupon-equivalent bill yields each declined 1 basis point to 3.68%, 3.69% and 3.69%. The 13-, 17- and 26-week yields held at 3.71%, 3.74% and 3.77%, while the 52-week rose 2 basis points to 3.82%. Pressure was greater in one-year paper and coupons than in the shortest cash instruments.

Treasury sold $69 billion of 119-day bills at a 3.635% high discount rate, equivalent to a 3.730% investment rate, with 3.15 bid-to-cover and 93.35% allotment at the high. Settlement is June 9. The scheduled liquidity buyback accepted the full $2 billion maximum in 20- to 30-year nominal coupons, from $21.26 billion offered across 14 of 36 eligible securities. The June 4 settlement remains ahead; the completed operation supports off-the-run liquidity without changing net borrowing policy.

The S&P 500 fell 0.74% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.29%, but semiconductors gained 1.39%, maintaining the sector's AI-related support. The VIX rose 1.84% to 16.06, a contained response. The dollar index gained 0.31% to 99.53 and gold fell 1.17% to $4,436.70. Higher real yields and a stronger dollar weighed across assets, without the volatility spike or short-bill disruption associated with a broad funding squeeze.

## AI Borrowing Expands as QXO Completes Its Financing

QXO's $6 billion financing for TopBuild drew more than three times the required demand. Its $3 billion, seven-year term loan received at least $6 billion of orders, with the spread tightened 25 basis points to 200 over the benchmark and the issue price improved to 99.75. The $3 billion bond portion attracted $14 billion: two $1.5 billion tranches due in 2031 and 2034 priced at par to yield 6.5% and 6.875%.

The bonds were rated BB- and the loan BB+. Scarce acquisition paper and anticipated scale benefits from the roughly $17 billion purchase helped QXO reduce financing costs despite those below-investment-grade ratings. JPMorgan was preparing another acquisition loan, $1.85 billion for Belden's purchase of Ruckus Networks, approximately matching the deal value. The commitment was complete, but the loan had not yet been placed with institutions.

AI funding was broadening well beyond individual data-center bonds. More than $370 billion of US high-grade, junk, loan and other AI-linked debt had been issued since the start of 2025. Participants at a New York credit forum reported strong demand, particularly where profitable hyperscalers support the obligation or principal amortizes. They were more cautious about underwriting based on hoped-for future growth.

Morgan Stanley's debt-capital-markets team estimated that AI could represent 10%-15% of all credit issuance during the year. The bank projected record US high-grade sales of $2.25 trillion, up from roughly $1.81 trillion, with hyperscalers expected to raise $250-$300 billion. Alphabet had already issued about $60 billion across dollars, Canadian dollars, euros, sterling, Swiss francs and yen. Access to several currencies reduces reliance on one buyer base, while increasing competition for capacity across bond, loan and project-finance markets.

Alphabet's planned participation in a $1 billion California prepaid-energy municipal deal opened another source of funding. Preliminary documents named it as funding recipient for debt expected to be rated Aa2 and used to obtain long-term discounted electricity for Pioneer Community Energy. The structure offers tax-exempt financing economics to the recipient and additional yield over similarly rated municipal bonds to investors. It would introduce a US technology company into a segment previously dominated by financial firms.

The arrangement could attract other hyperscalers seeking electricity for data centers, but the municipal market is much smaller than global corporate credit. Contract protections, counterparty strength and the depth of the buyer base would matter as the supply grows. Strong sponsorship cannot remove concentration in power demand or dependence on one financing structure.

Coastal GasLink was preparing a C$1 billion, two-part high-grade sale: approximately C$300 million at an 11.25-year maturity and C$700 million at about 19 years. Initial spreads were near 100 and 115 basis points over government bonds, respectively. Expected payments from maturing Canadian bonds could help demand, with final sizes and concessions still unconfirmed.

Other borrowers faced much harder terms. Merlin Entertainments had more than €720 million, about $838 million, of dollar and euro bonds maturing in November 2027. March net debt was about £5.4 billion, including £1.6 billion of leases. Weak Q1 earnings, heavy interest expense and pressure on household leisure spending had pushed some bonds toward distressed levels; the issuer was already rated CCC+.

Merlin's alternatives could include secured borrowing or an uptiering exchange. A more aggressive drop-down could place stronger Legoland assets beyond current creditors' reach. Sponsor backing and receptive high-yield markets improved the prospects for a transaction, but shifting priority would redistribute recoveries rather than fix weak earnings or high leverage.

Credit executives were also becoming more selective about software loans, flagging payment-in-kind exposure as sponsors developed defensive and offensive AI plans. Sleep Number was separately preparing for a possible bankruptcy filing and seeking financing that could become a debtor-in-possession loan. It had previously discussed a roughly $50 million rescue, with about $606 million of borrowings outstanding at the start of April. For such borrowers, the financing question was moving toward senior rescue capital rather than an ordinary refinancing.

The Fed reported a modest increase in 2025 bank-loan delinquencies across consumer, commercial and residential real estate categories, while banks remained well capitalized. Prominent nonbank defaults had also led lenders to revisit collateral management for private-market exposures. A different constraint came from Swiss institutions managing more than $270 billion, which planned to stop buying bonds from specified oil producers as existing holdings matured.

Listed funds weakened with the rise in government yields and softer risk tone: LQD fell 0.28%, HYG 0.28% and JNK 0.22%. QXO's completed deal showed that large transactions could still clear on improved terms. The distressed cases and changing investment mandates showed why that result could not be applied to every issuer.

## Inflation Pressures Persist Across Uneven Economies

Euro-area private activity contracted for a second month. The final composite PMI fell to 48.5 from 48.8, while services edged up to 47.7 from 47.6 but remained below 50. New orders weakened and employment losses accelerated, even as input and output prices rose faster.

Producer prices showed costs spreading beyond energy. April prices increased 0.6% on the month and 4.9% from a year earlier. Excluding energy, they rose 0.9% on the month, with intermediate goods up 1.8%, while energy prices fell 0.4%. Weak output could eventually limit tightening, but those broader cost increases complicated the ECB's ability to wait.

BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda said the June 15-16 meeting would need to weigh an increase if upside inflation risk outweighed the conflict's damage to activity. Markets assigned about an 85% chance to a quarter-point move. The yen traded near 160 per dollar despite a record ¥11.73 trillion of intervention between April 28 and May 27, as the rate gap with the US and the oil import bill continued to work against it.

Japan approved a ¥3.1 trillion supplementary budget, including a ¥2.5 trillion reserve initially intended to help cap gasoline costs. Deficit-financing bonds would fund it, but cancellation of previously planned issuance would keep total calendar-year supply unchanged. That avoided a direct increase in market supply, while subsidies, yen weakness and reduced BOJ purchases still complicated the inflation response. Higher domestic yields could also lessen Japanese institutions' appetite for currency-hedged foreign bonds; persistent currency weakness kept intervention and reserve management relevant.

Australian Q1 GDP rose only 0.3%, one-third of the previous quarter's pace and below expectations. Private investment nevertheless increased almost 4%, led by data centers, with machinery and equipment spending up 16%. Household spending and net exports were weaker. Three-year government yields retreated as markets leaned toward an RBA pause, although high unit labor costs and crude left room for another increase.

The Australian seven-year auction attracted bids exceeding four times the A$1 billion of November 2033 notes offered, the strongest cover for that maturity since its previous sale. The combination of softer growth and current yields brought buyers into intermediate maturities before the RBA had declared its tightening cycle complete.

Poland's Governor Adam Glapinski said the 3.75% policy rate was sufficiently high after May inflation of 3.1%, within the target band. Three-by-six-month forward-rate agreements traded 38 basis points above the three-month reference rate, down from 74 basis points of tightening priced after the war began. The remarks and reduced pricing added to the previous day's hold decision.

China's services index rose to 54.4 from 52.6 and its composite to 54.0 from 53.1. Demand improved, hiring resumed and input costs accelerated, but selling prices were broadly unchanged. The stronger activity offered a regional growth offset, with limited immediate evidence of prices being passed through to customers.

## Bahrain Reopens Gulf Funding as Sovereign Risks Diverge

Bahrain sold $1 billion of 10-year senior unsecured notes at 7.125%, just hours after intercepting Iranian missiles and drones. Orders peaked above $3.2 billion, allowing pricing 37.5 basis points inside initial guidance near 7.5%. It was the Gulf's first public sovereign bond since the war began.

Scarcity and expected regional support helped reopen funding without a durable ceasefire. Bahrain's own finances remained weak: debt around 140% of GDP, relatively low foreign-exchange reserves and almost no oil revenue with the Strait of Hormuz closed. Estimates pointed to roughly a 4% economic contraction and a deficit above 8% of GDP. A $5.4 billion currency swap with the UAE reinforced the support assumption, while the clearing yield showed the cost of access.

Argentina crossed its $10 billion annual dollar-purchase goal after the central bank bought another $43 million on Wednesday. Record crops, a 92% increase in energy exports and external borrowing by provinces and companies helped the inflows. Sovereign spreads narrowed alongside a recent Fitch upgrade, improving the immediate debt-service outlook.

Usable reserves were much smaller than gross acquisitions. Total reserves were just above $48 billion, but net reserves at market prices were estimated near $3 billion because purchased dollars had also financed debt payments. Argentina missed the net-reserve target in the latest review of its $20 billion IMF program, with more than $30 billion of payments due in 2027. Continued exports would extend the payment runway; rebuilding net reserves remained essential.

Zambia's creditor opposition became a blocking stake. Holders of more than 25% of the $1.36 billion 2053 bond prevented the cleanup call contemplated in the buyback. The notes traded near 81 cents, above the 78-cent offer. Retiring the debt before a potential coupon increase from 0.5% to 7.5% would lower future costs, with the step-up dependent on an IMF debt-sustainability condition being met in June and again in December. Above-offer trading and the blocking position made the negotiated terms more important.

India's funding pressure was spreading from bonds to banks. The 10-year government yield had risen 38 basis points to 7.04% since the conflict began, while domestic bond issuance fell 11% to 10.9 trillion rupees as companies sought cheaper loans. Bank credit grew 16.2% in the year through May 15, outpacing deposits; six-month certificate-of-deposit rates jumped 88 basis points in May. Corporate access was continuing, with more risk moving into short-term bank funding.

Officials were considering removing or sharply reducing the 20% tax on foreign investors' bond interest and lifting ownership caps on some securities. The rupee, down more than 6% during the year, closed at 95.71 per dollar; the 10-year was quoted at 7.02%. The proposals could attract a wider buyer base, but had not been approved and would not by themselves resolve oil, currency or bank-funding pressures.

Hungary's political rally had shifted toward delivery. Local-currency bonds had returned more than 11% since Peter Magyar defeated Viktor Orban, and the forint gained over 13% against the euro during the past year. Access to €16.4 billion of EU funding depended on completing projects by an August deadline. Potential rate cuts and eventual ratings action offered further support, while much of the foreign-debt benefit had already been priced.

Ghana's inflation rose for a second month to 3.7% from 3.4%, below the 4.3% median forecast. Fuel and fertilizer costs were lifting food prices, with an 11% year-to-date cedi decline adding imported pressure. Gross reserves of $14 billion covered 5.5 months of imports, giving the central bank room to smooth the currency's movement.

The government raised its 2026 growth forecast to more than 6% from 4.8%, citing lower inflation and rates and budget and foreign-exchange reforms. It expected year-end inflation of 5% rather than 8%. The improved baseline reflected progress since the 2022 default, but roughly $2 billion of annual energy-sector support and renewed food inflation still constrained public finances. The combination favored a continued 14% policy hold rather than assuming that stronger growth and reserves had removed inflation risk.

Broad EM dollar debt fell with the stronger dollar and higher oil: EMB lost 0.37%. The country cases showed the differences within that return, from Bahrain's expensive but successful sale to Argentina's reserve gains and the changing contractual and bank-funding pressures in Zambia and India.

## Forward Market Significance

Revised productivity, unit labor costs and initial claims are due June 4 at 08:30 ET, followed by the employment report June 5 at 08:30 ET and May CPI on June 10. The reference points are preliminary productivity growth of 0.8%, unit labor costs of 2.3%, the prior 215,000 claims reading, a payroll expectation of 93,000 and unemployment of 4.3%. Hiring and cost strength, followed by broad services or shelter inflation, would support the higher-real-rate pricing. Clear labor cooling and softer underlying prices would give more weight to the weak employment components in the services surveys.

Energy and policy decisions will determine how widely that pressure travels. The RBI meets June 5, the Bank of Canada June 10, the ECB the following week, the BOJ June 15-16 and the Fed June 16-17. Restored Strait of Hormuz traffic, lower crude and firmer currencies in energy-importing countries would allow more patient guidance. Further disruption or wider wage, services and expectations pressure would keep real yields and cross-border borrowing costs elevated.

June 4 brings Treasury announcements for the following week's 3-, 10- and 30-year coupons and 13- and 26-week bills. A cash-management buyback of up to $12.5 billion in one-month to two-year coupons runs from 13:40 to 14:00 ET, settling June 5. The 3-year auction follows June 9, with the 10-year reopening and another 17-week bill sale June 10. Alphabet's prepaid-energy financing and Coastal GasLink's two-part issue add corporate tests. Stable bill rates, smooth settlement and deals retaining planned sizes without large concessions would show that financing capacity remains available at the new rate level; weak bidding or cash pressure would make supply a more important driver of the next move.

section_summaries.summary: Services demand and higher oil lifted Treasury real yields despite mixed hiring signals. Bill auctions, buybacks and major corporate deals stayed orderly, while Bahrain demonstrated expensive but functioning sovereign access during conflict.

section_summaries.section_title: Services Demand Drives Real Yields Higher
section_summaries.summary: ISM demand outweighed weak employment components, and energy costs spread through businesses. Logan questioned policy restraint, Williams favored the current setting, and market pricing moved toward a more likely year-end hike.

section_summaries.section_title: AI Borrowing Expands as QXO Completes Its Financing
section_summaries.summary: QXO completed an oversubscribed acquisition package on better terms. AI debt expanded across markets, while Merlin, software lenders and Sleep Number highlighted leverage, collateral and rescue-financing risks.

section_summaries.section_title: Inflation Pressures Persist Across Uneven Economies
section_summaries.summary: Europe's weakening output coincided with broader cost inflation. Japan weighed a hike and funded energy relief without increasing calendar-year supply, while softer Australian growth attracted bond demand and China services strengthened.

section_summaries.section_title: Bahrain Reopens Gulf Funding as Sovereign Risks Diverge
section_summaries.summary: Bahrain reopened Gulf issuance on regional-support expectations. Argentina's dollar purchases outpaced usable-reserve gains; Zambia faced a blocking stake, and India's higher bond costs shifted pressure toward bank funding.

Labor-cost revisions, payrolls and CPI will test real-rate pricing. Energy flows, central-bank decisions, Treasury supply and new corporate structures will show how broadly policy and financing pressures spread.

overall_summary.headline: Real yields rise as services demand keeps Fed tightening in view
overall_summary.session_narrative:
The 10-year Treasury yield rose 3 basis points to 4.49%, with its real yield up 4 basis points and the breakeven down 1. ISM services reached 54.5 as orders and activity strengthened, despite contracting employment. ADP showed 122,000 additional private jobs. Oil rose again, and the Beige Book described costs spreading beyond fuel. By late trading, markets assigned more than an 80% chance to a year-end Fed increase.

Funding remained available. Treasury's bill auction drew solid demand and its long-end buyback accepted the full $2 billion cap. QXO's $6 billion acquisition financing was heavily subscribed and improved its terms. AI borrowing was reaching further into municipal and multi-currency markets, even as distressed borrowers faced possible priority changes and rescue financing.

Overseas, weak European activity did not stop producer costs rising, and Japan moved closer to a possible hike. Bahrain sold the Gulf's first public sovereign bond since the war began at a costly 7.125% yield. Argentina accumulated dollars but still needed net reserves, Zambia's creditor stake blocked a cleanup call, and Indian companies shifted financing toward banks. Labor, inflation and supply events will determine whether higher real yields can coexist with continued orderly financing.
overall_summary.summary: The Treasury selloff came through higher real yields despite a small decline in inflation compensation. Strong services demand and spreading energy costs outweighed weaker hiring details, while auctions and corporate financings continued to clear.
